comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed for the 2026-2027 intake from Utrecht University's current official overview, study-programme page and programme-specific 2026-2027 OER. The selected subject-specific track has a 127.5-EC major and 52.5-EC profiling space. The major consists of two compulsory 30-EC base packages; 7.5 EC Corpora en tools in de Neerlandistiek; a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis; one 30-EC depth package; two compulsory 7.5-EC cross-package depth courses; and one 7.5-EC method choice. The selected first-listed depth package is Nederlands: taal en gebruik, and the selected first-listed method option is Methods and Statistics 1. The 52.5-EC profiling space must include a coherent 30-EC profiling package but otherwise remains genuine choice space and is preserved generically. The 0-EC basisgrammatica test is a compulsory gate but does not create a credited component. 127.5 + 52.5 = 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. The current OER offers a Dutch-language subject-specific track and a partly English Crossing Borders track; the subject-specific track most directly represents the programme's Dutch-language-and-culture identity. Its two equally formal depth packages respectively emphasize language/use and Dutch-language literatures. Neither is clearly more general, so the first-listed package, Nederlands: taal en gebruik, is selected by official order. Methods and Statistics 1 is likewise the first-listed compulsory method option. These choices were fixed independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest match integrates Dutch language, literature, communication, identity, media and research. Two additional generator-backed directions are both coherent and feasible: Dutch Language, Communication & Digital Society, generated by language-use, acquisition, public communication, social variation and AI-related interests; and Dutch Literature, Culture & Social Questions, generated by literary, historical, transnational and socially engaged literature interests. Each pair differs by at least four courses: the closest and language routes differ by four courses (30 EC), the closest and literature routes by six (45 EC), and the two focused routes by ten (75 EC). The formal Crossing Borders direction is independently coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives has been reached.

alternatives.label: Dutch Language, Literature & Communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum balances Dutch-language literary and cultural analysis with rhetoric, stylistics, communication, media, psycholinguistics, digital methods and independent research.
alternatives.concept: A broad UCR response combining Dutch language use and communication, literary interpretation across periods and media, cultural identity, psycholinguistics, digital methods and qualitative and historical research.
progression: Introductory literature, rhetoric, Dutch communication, brain and behaviour, history, sociology, media, programming and research methods precede advanced literary, cultural, communication, data and psycholinguistic work. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Dutch Language, Communication & Digital Society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates on language acquisition and use, public and persuasive communication, media, social identity, AI ethics, data analysis and language technologies.
alternatives.concept: A language-use pathway centred on acquisition and psycholinguistics, rhetoric and persuasion, public and digital communication, social variation and identity, AI ethics, corpus/data methods and large-language-model technologies.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this pathway replaces four literature/history courses with AI ethics, advanced social theory, focused identity psychology and neural networks. The 30-EC change follows the evidenced emphasis on digital language, social variation, acquisition and institutional communication.
progression: Dutch communication, rhetoric, literature, brain and behaviour, sociology, history, media, programming, data science and research methods precede advanced social theory, persuasive communication, psycholinguistics and neural-network study. Introduction to Data Science precedes Neural Networks & Deep Learning; all planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Dutch Literature, Culture & Social Questions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by literary interpretation, media, historical context, cultural identity, adaptation, material circulation and socially engaged cultural analysis.
alternatives.concept: A literature-and-culture pathway centred on close reading, historical texts and identities, literary circulation across media, adaptation, climate and social questions, cultural institutions and creative communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces psycholinguistics, statistical methods, programming, data science, advanced history and one language-focused strand with media archaeology, environmental media, documentary and denser art-historical and literary research. Six courses differ (45 EC); it also differs by ten courses (75 EC) from the language-and-digital-society route.
progression: Introductory literature, film/media, rhetoric, Dutch communication, history, art history, sociology and qualitative methods precede advanced literary meaning, adaptation, documentary, media-and-race, creative communication and art-historical research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

notes.text: Utrecht provides a Dutch-language disciplinary sequence in Dutch linguistics, historical Dutch texts, Dutch-language literatures and cultures, corpus methods and a bachelor thesis. UCR can build closely related programmes through literature, communication, media, psycholinguistics, sociology, history and digital methods, including one Dutch-language course, but it does not reproduce a full Dutch philology or Neerlandistiek curriculum.

The comparator includes dedicated medieval and early-modern Dutch, comparative Dutch linguistics, multilingualism and literacy, Dutch corpus tools and a Dutch-language thesis. UCR offers adjacent analytical and research strengths but lacks those specialist Dutch-language components at the same depth.
